title: Three-slide win deck + risk brief for executive commit
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Overview:

This page contains a compact, reproducible three-slide executive deck plus an accompanying two-page risk brief designed to accelerate technical and commercial commitment conversations for Redwood Inference. Use it to:
- Surface the unit economics and measurable wins in the first 90 days.
- Address top technical and security objections proactively.
- Provide a clear commercial ask (pilot-to-commit).

When to use:
- CISO / CTO / VP Platform meetings where time is limited (15–30 minutes).
- Executive steering committees evaluating a pilot commitment.
- Pre-contract review to un-block legal or security gates.

Slide pack (three slides; each slide maps to a one-page speaking note):

Slide 1 — Business outcome & success metrics (30s):
- Headline: "Reduce inference unit cost by 40% while preserving P95 latency targets"
- One-paragraph value pitch with baseline: "Typical customer baseline: 4.2x token cost vs optimized runtime; Redwood pilot target: 40% cost reduction and SLO-aligned latency for 95% of requests."
- Key metrics (callouts):
  - Primary KPI: cost per 1k tokens (target pilot: $X.XX — see pricing guidance).
  - Availability SLO: 99.9% application-facing availability for hosted endpoints.
  - Latency objective: P95 <= 200ms for short text generation (<=512 tokens) on dedicated capacity.
  - Time-to-impact: expected measurable unit-cost improvement within 30 days (prefix caching + batching).

Slide 1 speaking note (one-paragraph):
Explain the measurable unit-economics: sample customer with 2M tokens/day saw 38% cost reduction after enabling caching + quantized model variant and switching cold paths to a lower-cost instance family. Emphasize tradeoffs (small quality delta <1% measured on eval set).

Slide 2 — Architecture, fallbacks, and risk mitigations (60s):
- Diagram (textual): "Client -> Redwood API -> Smart Router -> Model Pool (A: low-latency quantized vX, B: high-quality non-quantized vY) -> KV cache".
- Operational mitigations:
  - Canary rollout (5% traffic) then 25%/50%/100% with 24h guard rails.
  - Automated fallback policy: if P95 latency or error rate exceeds thresholds, route to alternate model variant or burst to Dedicated pool.
  - Observability hooks: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency heatmaps, tracing of request path.
- Security mitigations:
  - Data handling: in-hosted mode, customer data is isolated per-tenant; in Private mode, data never traverses Redwood control plane unless explicitly enabled.
  - Key management: integrates with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, HSM options).
  - Audit & compliance: request-level audit logs retained per contract (default 90 days, configurable).

Slide 2 speaking note (one-paragraph):
Call out the automatic downgrade/fallback behavior and the fact that we can run a private deployment for regulated workloads. Tie the fallback examples to real SLO thresholds (see runbook).

Slide 3 — Commercial ask & next steps (45s):
- Pilot scope (recommended): 4–8 week technical pilot with 30–90 days of production-like traffic shaping.
- Deliverables: measurable cost delta report, latency/throughput dashboard, small set of quality evals and regression alerts.
- Recommended commercial ask (executive-friendly): 
  1) Pilot credit: $25k service credit to cover engineering time + up to 1.5M tokens of covered usage.
  2) Commitment trigger: if pilot meets defined economic and quality thresholds, execute a 12-month reserved capacity agreement with an agreed monthly committed throughput.
- Next steps checklist (owner, timeline):
  1) Technical kickoff (owner: Solutions Eng) — within 3 business days of agreement.
  2) Baseline data share & traffic replay (owner: Customer Platform) — 5 business days for sample export.
  3) Pilot activation & 4-week measurement window (owner: Redwood Eng/Customer Eng).

Pricing guidance (pilot -> commit):
- Use this as executive reference. Numbers below are example guidance and should be adapted to the customer economics.

Monospace pricing table example (for slide handout):

"""
Tier             | Pilot (example)            | Commit (12m reserved)
-----------------|----------------------------|-------------------------
Included credits | $25,000 REDWOOD CREDIT      | n/a
Covered tokens   | up to 1.5M tokens          | volume-based discounts
Unit price (hosted) | $0.0035 / 1k tokens       | $0.0020–$0.0028 / 1k tokens (banded)
Dedicated uplift  | n/a                        | +% uplift for guaranteed capacity
On-prem / Private | engineering fee + setup    | platform license + support
"""

- Pilot pricing note: pilots are handled as non-recurring credits in most cases. If pilot uses Dedicated capacity, pilot monthly seat will be pro-rated and counted toward commit.

Risk brief (two pages — condensed):
- Top technical risks and mitigations:
  1) Quality regression: mitigate by running shadow quality evals and instant rollback. Threshold: if BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval degrades >1.5% on the critical prompt set, roll back to previous variant and notify customer.
  2) Latency spikes under burst: mitigate with burst capacity and auto-routing; guard at P95 > 500ms triggers fallback.
  3) Data residency concerns: offer Private deployment in VPC with customer-managed KMS and audit logs retained on customer storage.
  4) Cost overrun during ramp: apply per-route rate limits and token caps; Solutions Eng to configure quota alerts at 50%/80%/95%.

- Top legal / compliance risks and mitigations:
  - Data retention: default retention 90 days; customer can request shorter or self-host for zero retention.
  - Third-party model licensing: only deploy models with compatible licenses; our catalog indicates license types per model on onboarding docs.

Security FAQ for prospect CISO (short Q&A):
Q: Where is customer data stored and who can access it?
A: For hosted customers, data is stored in tenant-isolated backends in region; access is controlled by RBAC and audited. For Private deployments data remains in customer VPC. We provide a SOC2 Type II report for hosted control plane operations and will share additional artifacts under NDA.

Q: Can we bring our own keys?
A: Yes. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and support HSM-based wrapping on Private deployments.

Q: How do you prevent model updates from causing regressions?
A: We support pinned model versions and automated canary rollouts. Regression detection is tied to per-prompt eval suites; deviations trigger immediate rollback and alerting.

Q: What logging and telemetry do you provide for audits?
A: Request-level logs (timestamp, route, model version, token count, latency, outcome) and admin audit trails for configuration changes. Retention and export formats are configurable per contract.

Q: What scope of penetration testing and certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains quarterly internal pentests and engages third-party assessments annually. We provide SOC2 Type II attestation; ISO/IEC 27001 readiness is available on request.

How to use this page / deliverables: 
1) Export the three slides as PPTX using our standard slide template (folder: S3://redwood-sales/templates/3-slide-win.pptx).
2) Attach the two-page risk brief as an appendix to the commercial proposal.
3) Use the pricing table as a negotiation anchor; update unit prices to match current regional pricing before sending.

Ownership and escalation: 
- Primary owner: Go-to-market Solutions Engineering (contact: se-leads@redwood.ai)
- Escalation path: Account Executive -> Head of Solutions -> Legal & Security for contract exceptions.

Appendix: sample pilot acceptance criteria (to be adapted per customer):
- Economic: pilot shows >= 25% reduction in per-token cost vs customer baseline over a 14-day steady-state window.
- Quality: no measurable degradation on critical prompt set (max 1.0% delta on eval metric).
- Reliability: endpoint availability >= 99.9% during pilot; P95 latency under agreed threshold (default 200ms).
- Operational: customer has access to dashboards and critical alerts; runbook and rollback tested in-scope.
